text.p: The collapse of a building in eastern China's Zhejiang province has killed 36 people and injured three, local officials said on Tuesday.
Local authorities were still investigating the cause of the collapse on Saturday of the new residential building in Zhejiang's Changshan county, a police official said by telephone.
"Experts are hurrying here one after another," the official said.
The 36 residents were killed when the central section of the five-storey block collapsed, sending side walls tumbling in on top of the building's 30 apartments, the Workers' Daily newspaper said.

It took more than six hours for rescuers to pluck the first of the three injured survivors from the rubble of the block, a residential building built for employees of a local textile factory, it said.
Angry relatives of those killed were threatening to travel to Beijing to protest against the building's shoddy construction, the Hong Kong Standard newspaper said.
County officials had turned down a request from relatives for all the victims to be buried together and for a monument to be erected on the site, the newspaper said.
